title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals deployed AI-generated video and images to impersonate a real immigration attorney on social media, creating hundreds of fraudulent profiles that offered immigration services to vulnerable populations. The scam operated without any human verification of the purported attorney's identity, relying instead on AI-generated deepfakes and fabricated client testimonials to build false credibility. Catching this would have required social media platforms to verify the identity of accounts offering professional legal services before allowing them to operate.

The scheme targeted immigrants seeking legal assistance, extracting payments through digital transfer apps for services that were never provided. The victims lost thousands of dollars to fake contracts and false promises. It is not established whether the platforms had detection systems in place that failed, or whether such protections did not exist for this category of fraudulent activity.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using Leal's likeness to promote fraudulent immigration services. The scammers offer services like US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for payments of $2,200 or more, with some fake videos featuring supposed client testimonials praising Leal's services. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and the situation has dramatically worsened over the past three months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scammers typically direct victims to contact a phone number through WhatsApp, then send phony contracts and request payment via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scam's origins. He warns immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to avoid paying for immigration benefits through digital payment apps.
